claim: The reach caption describes 'All like this' as a mode whose edits go to every same-type peer as you make them.
truth: True for single-property edits only. Every control that writes more than one property at once — Spacing (padding/margin pairs, gap), Border (the shorthand batch), Flexbox and Grid — goes through handleBatchStyleChange, which never reads reachPeerIds. In 'All like this' mode those edits silently land on the selected element alone while the banner says twelve are being edited.

truth: The product has a lock and the inspector ignores it completely. A locked element cannot be clicked on canvas, but a Layers row click selects it with no guard, and from there every inspector control is live and every write lands — there is no read-only mode, no banner, no disabled state. So there is no distinct locked state to draw. Recording it so this is not re-audited; whether the inspector SHOULD respect the lock is a founder question, not a board fix.
evidence: Grep for `locked|isLocked` across packages/editor/src/editor/inspector returns two unrelated hits (a comment in tabs/InspectorTabContent.tsx:229 and a featureFlags comment). The lock exists: shared/types/element.ts:73-74, engine/elements/Element.ts:152-153 setLocked, engine/elements/ElementSerialization.ts:140-142 isLocked. Its consumers are canvas-only: editor/canvas/hooks/useSelectionBehavior.ts:88,106,134 (toast 'This element is locked. Unlock it in the Layers panel.'), canvas/overlays/SelectionBoxOverlay.tsx:87, canvas/menus/actions/standaloneActions.ts:108,120, insertActions.ts:69,90. The Layers row has no guard — editor/panels/layers/LayerTreeItem.tsx:143 `onSelect(layer.id, {})` on Enter/Space with no isLocked check (the file reads isLocked at :89 and uses it only for drag, rename and the lock glyph at :99,:146,:196,:327). No style-write path consults it: hooks/useStyleHandlers.ts, hooks/useBatchStyleHandler.ts, engine/styles/StyleEngine.ts and engine/elements/ElementStyles.ts contain no lock read.
edit: No board. Raise as a founder question: should the inspector go read-only on a locked element, or should the Layers row refuse to select one?
